TVP_POPULATIONS_OF_INTEREST: Moderate-severe IBD: Crohn’s Disease 600K patients in the US, 400K patients in the EU; Ulcerative Colitis 660K patients in the US, 600K patients in the EU.
TVP_NEED:
Available therapies have low remission rates, lack durable remission, and many have significant safety concerns.  Only 25-40% of biologic-naïve patients achieve remission at induction (8-12 weeks).  And only 20-30% of patients will achieve and maintain remission at year 1.  Chronic illness and unpredictable flares lead to 50% of bio-treated patients receiving steroids and recurring hospitalizations.  

Patients cycle through “conventional treatments”, such as amino-salicylates (5 ASAs) and corticosteroids, before progressing to advanced treatment. Conventional therapies are less effective in Crohn’s vs UC, so Crohn’s patients move to advanced therapy faster.  TNF biologics maintain over 50% share in 1L advanced therapy before moving to other classes (biologic α4β7, biologic IL-23, biologic IL-12/23, oral JAK).
TVP_COMPETITIVE_POSITIONING_CURRENT_SOC: Potential for high efficacy oral in 2L. Superior treatment for CD & UC control, fast onset of action, and improved mucosal healing vs SOC for patients not well controlled by or intolerant to current therapeutics including biologics.

Only ~50% of patients have mucosal recovery 1 year or later after diagnosis and many patients with celiac disease report having persistent symptoms despite adherence to the gluten-free diet
